correctness.rationale: The elementary syndromes are ±x_i and ±z_i. The consecutive pairing uses each antipodal class on each projective line exactly once. Every wedge x_i∧z_i vanishes and the columns span, giving an isotropic rank-r stabilizer. Every nonzero joint-Lee error of weight at most two is a difference of distinct radius-one errors, so none lies in the centralizer. The coordinate with pair (1,2) supplies X_i Z_i² of weight three and syndrome zero. Removing that coordinate leaves at least all other projective lines, which outnumber the lines in a hyperplane by p^(r−1)−1>0, so no stabilizer is supported there. Conversely, in a perfect nonempty coordinatewise-collinear code every syndrome is nonzero except the identity's, and each coordinate uses exactly two antipodal classes on a unique line. Thus (p−1)/2 must be even. This counts within the stipulated frame and does not give an obstruction for noncollinear checks.
residual_risks: Finite replay checks the pairing and syndrome space, not the universal logical-distance or necessity arguments. Usual nonempty block length is implicit in the converse.

value.rationale: The useful result is a restricted-class classification in a fixed joint-Lee frame: it gives a uniform nondegenerate construction saturating the packing bound and a necessary constraint for designs with locally proportional checks. This is useful beyond merely evaluating the bound or reprinting the first parameter example, and the simple termwise commutativity makes the distinction from noncollinear global-cancellation designs precise.
residual_risks: No value assigned for the already-known six-qudit parameters, ordinary Hamming distance, efficient correction, or a nonexistence result outside the collinear class.
